chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Muʿāwiyah ibn Ḥukaym, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from a righteous man, peace be upon him, who said:

I asked him about a man who doubts and does not know whether he has prayed one, or two, or three, or four; his prayer becomes confused for him. He said: “All of that?” He said: I said: “Yes.” He said: “Then let him proceed in his prayer and seek refuge in Allah from al-Shayṭān al-Rajīm, for it is likely soon to go away from him.”

The proper understanding of this report is one of two possibilities. One of them is that we interpret it as applying to a supererogatory prayer, for there is nothing in the report indicating that he doubted in an obligatory prayer. The second possibility is that what is meant is one whose forgetfulness is frequent and who is unable to guard against it; it is permissible for him to proceed in his prayer, because if repetition were made obligatory upon him while forgetfulness is his condition, he would never be free of prayer in any state. As for one whose doubt occurs only sometimes, then repetition is obligatory upon him according to what we have stated before; that is indicated by this.

key_terms.النَّافِلَةِ: the supererogatory prayer as opposed to the obligatory prayer
key_terms.سَهْوُهُ: his forgetfulness or recurring inattentiveness in prayer
key_terms.صَلَاتُهُ: his salat (prayer), the act of worship under discussion
key_terms.فَلْيَمْضِ: let him continue and proceed without breaking the prayer
key_terms.وَلْيَتَعَوَّذْ: let him seek refuge in Allah
key_terms.يَشُكُّ: he doubts regarding the number of units prayed

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he doubts how many rakʿahs he has prayed?
ai.summary: This report addresses the ruling concerning doubt in the number of rakʿahs during salat (prayer). It instructs proceeding in the prayer and seeking refuge in Allah, while the accompanying explanation clarifies that this is understood either about supererogatory prayer or about a person whose forgetfulness is frequent, whereas occasional doubt requires repetition according to the earlier ruling.
